sides.says: Ground 25, coupler 60, input 15, output 15 mm deploys the fin 0-92 deg.

The record (four_bar_military_data) closes at every pose, self-checks every link length, and survives worst-case plus/minus 0.15 mm tolerances. The historical sweep stays committed as the failure record.
discrepancies.resolved_by: Engineering redesign by the chief weapons engineer under the sponsor's Phase 1 direction, 2026-11-14; analytical, software-tested, no physical mechanism observed.

discrepancies.title: Reference and textbook fin-term formulations disagree about the static-margin window

sides.says: Fin CP sweep term uses the root chord; margin 1.55-1.57 cal (inside 1.5-2.0).
Textbook Barrowman sweep term (tip leading-edge sweep X_R) and mid-chord line length give 0.74-0.76 cal (outside 1.5-2.0).

discrepancies.found_by: Independent re-derivation of the fin terms during the 2026-09-28 review.
discrepancies.next_action: None for the record; the physical CG measurement is tracked by PRED-C5-DRY-CG.
discrepancies.resolution: Phase 1: the reference script was WRONG and the textbook cross-check was right. The revision-2 script used the root chord where the tip leading-edge sweep X_R belongs in the fin CP term, and the sweep length where the mid-chord line length belongs in the normal-force term; both errors pushed the CP aft and inflated the margin to a false 1.55-1.57 cal (true value about 0.7 cal at the old geometry). Revision 3 uses the textbook terms, and an independent strip-integration cross-check now agrees with the closed form within 0.001 mm (CP) and 0.01 percent (CN). Fins were resized so the margin is 1.69-1.78 cal.
discrepancies.resolved_by: Formulation correction in Simulation/static_margin.py rev 3 plus numerical cross-check, 2026-11-14; analytical, software-tested.

discrepancies.title: The reliability simulation cannot produce the failures it counts

sides.says: omega_final is forced to 0 when the toggle event fires; k (N*m/rad) is applied as a constant torque (N*m); latency shifts start time only.
10,000 of 10,000 trials succeed.

discrepancies.found_by: Reading the success criterion against the integrator's event handling.
discrepancies.next_action: None for the record; physical deployment trials are tracked by PRED-C7-LOCK-FRACTION.
discrepancies.resolution: The reliability simulation was rebuilt: the fin equation of motion is integrated through the verified four-bar kinematics (spring torque on the crank, angle-of-attack-dependent aero, friction), and link tolerances enter through a numerically derived toggle gradient. Every counted failure mode can occur. In 10,000 seeded trials, 9,993 succeed (99.93 percent); the 7 failures are all stop-angle tolerance tail, honestly labeled.
discrepancies.resolved_by: Simulation rebuild in Simulation/reliability_sweep.py rev 2 at design_point.json, 2026-11-14; software-tested.

discrepancies.title: Laminate modulus is below the aluminium comparison

sides.says: Claim: match or exceed aluminium stiffness; relies on increased section thickness.
Ex = 56.68 GPa, below 69.0 GPa.

discrepancies.found_by: Requirement R-C8-MODULUS evaluated from the CLT output.
discrepancies.next_action: Coupon or component stiffness measurement if a CFRP fin is ever made (Phase 6 option).
discrepancies.resolution: The equal-mass section-stiffness calculation the historical note relied on is now committed (structures/fea_lite.py, docs/EVIDENCE/C8_equal_mass_stiffness.json): at equal areal mass the 4.0 mm quasi-isotropic CFRP fin section is 4.28x stiffer in bending than the 2.28 mm 7075-T6 section of the same mass. The raw material-modulus comparison (56.68 vs 69 GPa) understates the structural trade, which is why R-C8-MODULUS is kept honestly unmet on its own terms while the component-stiffness question is answered.
discrepancies.resolved_by: Phase 4 equal-mass plate-bending calculation, 2026-11-14; analytical, software-tested.

discrepancies.title: Architecture diagram omitted the rocket's fins-deployed ignition gate

discrepancies.found_by: Reading the IGNITE branch in processSerialCommands().

discrepancies.title: Ignition requires deployed fins, but deployment requires a boost-level acceleration

sides.says: Deploy fires only after a >15 g x-axis reading while not IDLE; IGNITE is refused unless the deploy flag is set.
After sending IGNITE the launcher waits 5 s for IGNITED, then aborts.

discrepancies.found_by: Tracing the nominal command sequence through both firmwares.
discrepancies.next_action: None for the record; the 6.1 gate bench-validates the arming chain as designed.
discrepancies.resolution: Design decision (chief weapons engineer under the sponsor's Phase 4/6 direction): the PRIMARY ignition path is the launcher-side electric initiator (MIL-DEV-006), which lights the motor without any rocket command. The rocket then senses the sustained >=2 g launch event, deploys fins (~200 ms), and its fins-deployed gate on the rocket-side IGNITE servo path becomes an intentional extra interlock rather than a deadlock: the rocket-side servo is the BACKUP path, used only after a launch has already been detected (fins deployed), exactly when its gate passes. The wartime sequence is therefore: operator fire command -> launcher initiator -> acceleration -> fin deployment -> fuze S&A events. The launcher 5 s IGNITED-wait observes the rocket's IGNITED line, which the rocket emits from its own FLIGHT transition.
discrepancies.resolved_by: Design decision recorded by the chief weapons engineer, 2026-11-14, under the sponsor's militarization authority; documented in docs/MILITARY/FUZE.md and the operator card. The firmware gates themselves are unchanged.
discrepancies.progress: Phase 1 (MIL-DEV-010): the deploy trigger was re-derived for rail launch (2.0 g sustained 150 ms) because the G64W cannot produce the historical 15 g on this mass. The ignition-vs-deployment ordering question itself remains open and must be resolved by the Phase 6 live-fire program design.

discrepancies.title: A launcher abort leaves an armed rocket armed, and the launcher cannot re-arm it

sides.says: abortSequence returns the launcher to SAFE and sends the rocket nothing. Re-arming waits for a rocket READY line and aborts with Rocket Timeout after 8 s.
sysState moves IDLE, ARMED, IGNITING, FLIGHT with no path back, so only a restart returns it to IDLE. READY is sent only in IDLE, and the deploy trigger stays live in any non-IDLE state.

discrepancies.found_by: Tracing the abort path through both firmwares while building the ground status model. Source reading only; not observed on hardware.
discrepancies.next_action: A human decides the intended behavior under a separate safety review, for example a disarm command sent on abort. No gate was changed. Until then the status board raises W-ARMED-AFTER-ABORT, and an aborted rocket should be treated as armed until it is restarted.
discrepancies.progress: docs/SAFETY.md now warns before the preflight steps that arm the rocket, and Firmware/preflight_audit.py flags a rocket still active after an abort. Firmware is unchanged.

discrepancies.title: The roll correction has no guard for a near-vertical rocket

sides.says: The comment above the accelerometer band says atan2 of near-zero axes is noise. The band tests total acceleration only, so a stationary rocket pointing straight up passes it, and roll is corrected from atan2(ay, az) while ay and az are both near zero.
[FUSION] Pitch is atan2(-ax, hypot(ay, az)) from the same relayed values, so ay and az total g*cos(pitch) when stationary, and error on them is magnified by 1/cos(pitch).

discrepancies.found_by: Reading the roll estimator while adding the status board's roll reference. A software port of the equations, with invented noise of 0.012 and 0.05 m/s^2 and an invented 2 ms loop, gave a roll standard deviation of 0.08 to 0.35 deg at 5 deg from vertical and 0.4 to 1.8 deg at 1 deg, with excursions of 67 deg exactly at vertical. Not observed on hardware; sensor noise and loop period are not measured.
discrepancies.next_action: A human decides whether firmware should also gate on the size of ay and az, under review because canard output depends on roll in FLIGHT. No firmware was changed. Until then the status board raises A-ROLL-REFERENCE-WEAK within 5 deg of vertical. An inert capture held near vertical would show the real size.

discrepancies.title: P-003 as first proposed could not see gyro drift, because the accelerometer holds roll in that pose

sides.says: While stationary near 1 g, every loop sets roll to 0.98 (roll + rate dt) + 0.02 accel roll, so a residual gyro bias b settles at an offset of 49 b dt instead of growing. Roll runs on the gyro alone only in boost, coast, and FLIGHT.
P-003 reads roll_deg from LOG rows over 600 s, stationary and level, to report drift.

discrepancies.found_by: Reading the roll estimator. A software port of the equations with an invented 1 deg/s bias and 2 ms loop ended 600 s at 0.10 deg, matching 49 b dt, against 600 deg on the gyro alone. Not observed on hardware.
discrepancies.next_action: A human reviews the revised P-003 before registering it. It now also integrates rate_deg_s from the same LOG rows, which reads the gyro without the correction and needs no firmware change.
